institution: Sendai District Court
what_happened: A woman who had undergone sterilization under the former Eugenic Protection Law filed a State Redress Act damages action against the national government.
result_or_next_step: The filing made the contemporary judicial remedy pathway formally observable; the litigation proceeded through appeals.

institution: National Diet of Japan
what_happened: The Diet enacted the 2019 lump-sum payment law for people who had undergone eugenic surgery under the former law.
result_or_next_step: Most provisions took effect the same day, creating a national 3.2 million yen lump-sum payment pathway.

institution: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and prefectural governments
what_happened: The Ministry issued implementation instructions for claims, ministerial recognition, prefectural receipt, and payment under the 2019 law.
result_or_next_step: The statutory lump-sum remedy entered administrative operation through national and prefectural procedures.

institution: Supreme Court of Japan, Grand Bench
what_happened: The Grand Bench held the former law's eugenic-surgery provisions unconstitutional and the related legislative conduct unlawful under the State Redress Act.
result_or_next_step: The Court rejected the government's exclusion-period defense in the Sendai case and recognized a basis for state liability, followed by executive and legislative responses.

institution: Prime Minister of Japan and Government of Japan
what_happened: The Prime Minister met plaintiffs and affected people, apologized on behalf of the government, and stated directions for resolving pending litigation and creating a new compensation framework.
result_or_next_step: The government began work on settlements and a broader compensation response with the cross-party Diet group.

institution: National Diet of Japan
what_happened: The Diet unanimously passed a new compensation law whose preamble acknowledged responsibility in light of the 2024 Supreme Court judgments.
result_or_next_step: The law was promulgated on 2024-10-17 and scheduled to take effect on 2025-01-17, creating compensation and revised lump-sum pathways.

institution: Children and Families Agency, prefectural governments, and recognition commission
what_happened: The 2024 compensation law took effect and official claim reception began through prefectural windows under national recognition and payment procedures.
result_or_next_step: Claims, recognitions, and payments continue through the national and prefectural administrative process.

institution: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
what_happened: The first stage of the amended livelihood-assistance standards became applicable after the Ministry's 2013-05-16 notice stated that the revised standards would apply from this date.
result_or_next_step: The disputed revision entered administrative operation; later stages through 2015 are retained within this origin Episode rather than split into additional Episodes.

institution: Osaka High Court
what_happened: On appeal in the selected Osaka pathway, the High Court reversed the District Court's cancellation of the benefit-modification decisions and dismissed the plaintiffs' appeal on their damages claims.
result_or_next_step: The plaintiffs sought Supreme Court review, continuing the same judicial pathway within the Judicial Line.

institution: Nagoya High Court
what_happened: On appeal in the selected Nagoya pathway, the High Court ruled against the national government and municipalities after the District Court had dismissed the claims.
result_or_next_step: The national government and municipalities sought Supreme Court review, continuing the same judicial pathway within the Judicial Line.

institution: Supreme Court of Japan, Third Petty Bench
what_happened: In the Osaka case, the Court held the revision unlawful under the Public Assistance Act because the deflation adjustment used price change alone without an adequately grounded expert process.
result_or_next_step: The Court cancelled the Osaka claimants' benefit-modification decisions but rejected their State Redress Act damages claims against the national government.

institution: Supreme Court of Japan, Third Petty Bench
what_happened: In the Nagoya case, the Court held the revision unlawful under the Public Assistance Act because the deflation adjustment used price change alone without an adequately grounded expert process.
result_or_next_step: The Court cancelled the Nagoya claimants' benefit-modification decisions but rejected their State Redress Act damages claims against the national government.

institution: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
what_happened: The Ministry published the government's response direction: ordinary additional public-assistance payments would use the same revised adjustment for plaintiffs and non-plaintiffs, while plaintiffs would also receive a budget-funded special payment reflecting the litigation history.
result_or_next_step: The administrative response design moved to funding and implementation arrangements.

institution: National Diet of Japan
what_happened: The Diet completed approval of the FY2025 supplementary budget, which included expenditure identified by the Ministry for implementing the additional-payment response to the Supreme Court judgments.
result_or_next_step: Budget authorization enabled the government to proceed with the payment framework; this Episode records approval of expenditure, not enactment of a new compensation statute.

institution: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and local public-assistance authorities
what_happened: The special public-assistance standard became applicable and Ministry instructions placed additional-payment calculation and delivery into local administrative operation.
result_or_next_step: Payments for current recipients began sequentially without an application as authorities became ready; former recipients use a request procedure with the authorities that provided their assistance.

institution: Minister of Justice and Legislative Council
what_happened: The Minister of Justice referred Question No. 129 on the rules governing criminal retrial procedures to the Legislative Council, which assigned the inquiry to a newly established criminal-law subcommittee.
result_or_next_step: The subcommittee began formal review of evidence production, appeals from retrial-opening decisions, judicial disqualification, and other procedural rules.

institution: Legislative Council
what_happened: After its retrial subcommittee held 18 meetings, the Council adopted the response to Question No. 129 by majority and submitted it immediately to the Minister of Justice.
result_or_next_step: The response recommended statutory rules for evidence-production orders, judicial disqualification, the structure of retrial-request review, extended appeal filing periods, and related matters, providing the basis for government bill preparation.

institution: Cabinet and Ministry of Justice
what_happened: The Cabinet approved and submitted a bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act's retrial procedures.
result_or_next_step: The government bill entered Diet consideration with proposed rules on evidence-production orders, appeals, judicial disqualification, screening and adjudication procedures, and related matters.

institution: National Diet of Japan
what_happened: The House of Councillors passed the government bill after House of Representatives amendment, completing enactment of the criminal-retrial procedure reform.
result_or_next_step: The amended law was promulgated on 2026-07-24 as Act No. 67 of 2026, with staged commencement provisions rather than immediate full entry into force.

institution: National Diet of Japan (Act No. 67 of 2026)
what_happened: The first group of amendments entered force 20 days after promulgation, including conditions and 14-day filing periods for appeals from specified retrial-related decisions and government publication duties.
result_or_next_step: The principal rules on evidence production, retrial-request screening and adjudication, judicial disqualification, and other procedures remain pending a Cabinet-order commencement date within one year of promulgation.
